questions.q: Why does Nimbus Mobile's requirement call for a single skills-based routing model instead of separate queues per channel (voice, chat, SMS, social)?
options: Because the business explicitly wants routing decided by agent skill and availability regardless of which channel a customer used
Because separate queues per channel are not technically possible in Salesforce
Because voice and chat cannot both be handled by the same agent under any configuration
Because skills-based routing is only available for a single channel at a time
questions.explain: The scenario's stated requirement is channel-agnostic, skill-based routing — Omni-Channel is built to treat work items from any channel the same way once they reach the router.

questions.q: Why is the outage-alert requirement modeled as an event-driven broadcast rather than a routed Case?
options: Because Cases cannot be created quickly enough for any urgent scenario
Because outage alerts are never time-sensitive
Because the alert is a broadcast to many active agents at once, triggered by an external monitoring event, not a one-to-one customer interaction waiting for a single agent
Because Omni-Channel does not support voice interactions
questions.explain: Routing is built for one customer interaction matched to one agent; a broadcast to many active sessions at once triggered by an external event is a different shape of problem, which is why an event-driven pattern fits and routing it as a Case would not.

questions.q: Why does the design move older interaction history into a large-data-volume storage pattern instead of keeping everything as standard Case records indefinitely?
options: Because standard Case records automatically delete themselves after 90 days

Because storage costs and query performance both degrade as millions of monthly interactions accumulate, so recent operational data stays in standard objects while older history moves to a pattern built for scale
Because large-data-volume storage is the only way to ever view a Case record
Because compliance requires deleting all interaction history after one year
questions.explain: The reasoning is a scale and cost trade-off: keep what day-to-day operations actively query in standard objects, move what doesn't need always-on indexing into a storage pattern designed for very large historical volumes.

questions.q: Why does the legacy case-history migration need a different API approach than the live, day-one interaction traffic?
options: Because bulk APIs and real-time APIs are actually interchangeable for every use case
Because legacy data cannot be loaded into Salesforce under any circumstances
Because live traffic should also be loaded using the same bulk batch tool used for migration
Because the migration is a one-time, very large batch job best suited to bulk/batch tooling, while live traffic is individual records created continuously, which fits the real-time API path instead
questions.explain: Matching the tool to the job matters: large one-time historical loads fit batch-oriented bulk tooling, while continuous live customer interactions fit the real-time transactional path.

questions.q: What does Service Cloud Voice specifically contribute to this design?
options: It replaces the need for Omni-Channel routing entirely
It is exclusively a tool for outbound marketing calls
It brings telephony into the same console and routing engine as the other service channels, so voice is treated as just another routable work item
It only supports SMS, not actual phone calls
questions.explain: Service Cloud Voice's role is unifying voice into the same console and routing engine used for chat, SMS, and social, so agents aren't juggling separate systems per channel.
